methods.label: Principal roots and absolute values
methods.explanation:
The square root symbol gives the nonnegative root, so \(\sqrt{u^2}=|u|\). Since \(x<0\), we have \(x-1<0\), giving
\[
\sqrt{(x-1)^2}=|x-1|=1-x.
\]
Therefore the expression is
\[
\left|x-(1-x)\right|=|2x-1|.
\]
Because \(2x-1<0\), its absolute value is \(-(2x-1)=1-2x\). The answer is \(\boxed{1-2x}\), choice B.
